boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented CSUSB study environments, from quiet library seating and reservable rooms to computer-equipped workspaces for group, individual, and technical projects.

cards.title: Settle In at The Cave
cards.subtitle: A 24/7 study area in the Pfau Library Wedge
cards.notes: Bring your Coyote ID for secured periods, then use the workstations, whiteboards, outlets, or collaboration tables for a long session.
cards.short_summary: A round-the-clock workspace with computers and collaborative study equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB identifies The Cave as a 24/7 first-floor Library Wedge study area with more than 50 PC and Mac workstations, whiteboards, outlets, collaboration tables, vending machines, and microwaves.
cards.source_title: Open Computer Labs | Information Technology Services | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily. A Coyote ID in a mobile wallet or on a physical card is required during secured evening, overnight, and Sunday periods listed by ITS.

cards.entity_name: Pfau Library Wedge Computer Lab PL-1109
cards.title: Work at a Computer in PL-1109
cards.subtitle: A 24/7 self-service lab in the Library Wedge
cards.notes: Use PL-1109 when an assignment needs a campus computer; have your Coyote ID and CSUSB password ready to sign in at a station.
cards.short_summary: A continuously open computer lab for coursework requiring a campus workstation.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB lists Pfau Library Wedge room PL-1109 as a San Bernardino campus self-service computer lab operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Open Computer Labs | Information Technology Services | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily. Students sign in to lab stations with their Coyote ID and CSUSB password; secured Cave entry rules may apply when approaching through that area.

cards.title: Build a Weekday Work Block in PL-1003
cards.subtitle: A scheduled computer lab inside Pfau Library
cards.notes: Choose PL-1003 for computer-based coursework during posted weekday hours, and check the ITS page again because summer schedules may differ.
cards.short_summary: A library computer lab suited to focused, workstation-based assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB lists Pfau Library Lab PL-1003 as an open computer lab, with posted Monday-through-Friday hours and a notice that summer hours may vary.
cards.source_title: Open Computer Labs | Information Technology Services | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: The current ITS listing shows Monday–Thursday 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. and Friday 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; summer hours may vary.

cards.entity_name: Jack H. Brown College Open Computer Lab JB-123
cards.title: Take Computer Work to JB-123
cards.subtitle: A weekday lab in the business college building
cards.notes: Head to JB-123 when your study plan needs a desktop station near Jack H. Brown College classes; confirm seasonal hours before going.
cards.short_summary: A weekday computer workspace convenient to the business college.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB lists room JB-123 in the Jack H. Brown College of Business and Public Administration as a San Bernardino campus open computer lab.
cards.source_title: Open Computer Labs | Information Technology Services | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: The current ITS listing shows Monday–Thursday 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. and Friday 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; summer hours may vary.

cards.title: Move Quiet Work to the Fifth Floor
cards.subtitle: The library’s recommended floor for quiet study
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from fewer group conversations; the library specifically directs quiet-study seekers to this floor.
cards.short_summary: A library floor explicitly recommended for quieter individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library’s FAQ recommends the fifth floor for quiet studying because it has no group seating areas and tends to be quieter than other library spaces.
cards.source_title: Where is a quiet place to study? | Pfau Library FAQ
cards.access_notes: Use during Pfau Library building hours. This is an open floor rather than a reservable room; consult the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Gather a Larger Team in PL-111
cards.subtitle: A 14-seat reservable collaboration room
cards.notes: Reserve PL-111 for a larger team or remote participant, keep the confirmation email, and arrive within ten minutes of the start time.
cards.short_summary: A larger group room with seating and videoconferencing support.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library states that Meeting/Collaboration Room PL-111 is next to Starbucks, seats 14, supports videoconferencing, and can be reserved through its study-room system.
cards.source_title: Reserve Study Rooms | John M. Pfau Library | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: Reservation requires a MyCoyote login. Book up to four half-hour slots, retain the confirmation email, and occupy the room within ten minutes of the start time.

cards.entity_name: Pfau Library Smart Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Put Group Work on the Big Screen
cards.subtitle: Five reservable rooms with wireless display equipment
cards.notes: Book one for a group presentation or shared document review, then bring a compatible device to transmit work to the room’s large display.
cards.short_summary: Technology-equipped rooms for collaborative review and presentation practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library documents five VETI-funded Smart Group Study Rooms, each with a 65-inch flat-screen monitor and an AirServer unit for transmitting from a personal device.
cards.source_title: Reserve Study Rooms | John M. Pfau Library | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: These are group rooms for two or more people. Reserve with a MyCoyote account up to one week ahead and arrive within ten minutes of the booked start.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for Solo Focus
cards.subtitle: Ten reservable individual study rooms on the fourth floor
cards.notes: Schedule a private work block up to one week ahead, save the confirmation email, and arrive promptly so the reservation is not forfeited.
cards.short_summary: Reservable fourth-floor rooms intended for one-person study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library states that ten individual study rooms on the fourth floor can be reserved in advance and identifies the individual room type as seating one person.
cards.source_title: Reserve Study Rooms | John M. Pfau Library | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: For one person only. Reserve with a MyCoyote login for up to four half-hour slots, as far as one week ahead, and retain the confirmation email.

cards.entity_name: Geospatial Engagement and Learning Lab Rooms
cards.title: Run Mapping Work in a GEL Lab Room
cards.subtitle: Four reservable rooms for geospatial projects
cards.notes: Reserve a GEL room when coursework calls for ArcGIS or spatial analysis, and plan for no more than two people at its high-performance computer.
cards.short_summary: Small reservable rooms equipped for mapping and spatial-analysis assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library says four Geospatial Engagement and Learning Lab study rooms seat two people and provide high-performance computers with ArcGIS and other spatial-mapping software.
cards.source_title: Reserve Study Rooms | John M. Pfau Library | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: Each room seats two. Reserve through the library system with a MyCoyote login, keep the confirmation email, and arrive within ten minutes.

cards.title: Share a Table in PL-503
cards.subtitle: A non-reservable fifth-floor room for multiple groups
cards.notes: Try PL-503 when advance booking is not practical, choose an open table, and arrive prepared to share the room with other working groups.
cards.short_summary: A shared group-study room available without advance reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library identifies PL-503 as a Multi-Group Study Room with several tables, says it cannot be reserved, and requires groups to share while a table remains unoccupied.
cards.source_title: Reserve Study Rooms | John M. Pfau Library | CSUSB
cards.access_notes: No advance reservation is available. Use is subject to Pfau Library building hours, and occupants must share the room while an unoccupied table is available.
